references.text: Basic regulations concerning the Day of Atonement (Yom Kippur) on the tenth day of the seventh month, where the people must humble themselves and refrain from work.
Parallel text describing the Day of Atonement, with a command for a holy assembly, self-denial, and rest from all labor.
The tenth day of the seventh month is also mentioned in connection with the Jubilee year, when the trumpet was to sound on the Day of Atonement.
Isaiah speaks about humbling one's soul and fasting, which highlights the significance of self-denial on the Day of Atonement.
David describes how he humbled his soul with fasting, illustrating the practice of self-denial.
Acts refers to 'the fast' (νηστεία), which is a reference to the Day of Atonement in Jewish tradition.
Hebrews describes how the high priest entered the Most Holy Place once a year, an event that took place on the Day of Atonement.
Hebrews mentions the annual reminder of sins, referring to the rituals of the Day of Atonement.
